display.title: Hashem Figures It Out On His Own
display.summary_short: A poor rav who needs money for his daughters' weddings refuses to travel to his rich brother, trusting Hashem instead, and help arrives in a way no one could have planned.
display.summary_long: The storyteller opens with a lesson on bitachon: we do not need to work out how Hashem will help, because nature itself is His creation. He recalls the Gemara's story of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's daughter, whose Shabbos candles burned on vinegar. The story follows Reb Avraham, a Chassid of the Chozeh of Lublin and the rav of a small, poor town in Poland. His wife worries about paying for their daughters' weddings, but he will not ask the struggling townspeople for a raise. She urges him to travel a hundred miles to his rich brother in Moscow. He sets out, but returns at once with three questions: is his brother still alive, is he still rich, and will he give? Hashem, he says, is always alive, always rich and always kind. Days later a burly poritz leaves a sack of gold coins in his care, saying that if he does not return in ten days the money is theirs. Months later, unsure, the rav asks the Chozeh of Lublin, who tells him to use the gift Hashem sent.
display.lesson: Trust in Hashem without trying to figure out how He will help; He is always alive, always rich and always kind.

characters: the poritz with the sack of gold
